section: Iterate — change: R1c-3 recognisers see both places
title: Every recogniser of a moving root file sees it in both places; labels use name() (R1c-3)
context: After R1c-2 every reader and writer found a moving file through path(), but sets, a regex, project markers, a git pathspec and phase hints still recognised it by its root name, so after R3 a moved file would be misclassified (derived snapshot, sensitive path, FR coverage, project detection).
decision: Recognisers ask the registry for every known location (known_rels / all_known_rels); readers that report a place report the resolved one; pure labels use name(); change_type_paths judges a moved root file as the root file it is. Skip-safety stays root-only because it loosens the required review gate. An AST net forbids rel()/legacy_rel() of a moving or computed key in production code.
consequences: Unmigrated repos behave as before: sets only gain paths that do not exist. The safety window of BRIEF 12.12 (b) ends. R3 must switch skip-safety and narrow the design/plan boundary prefixes with the move (BRIEF 12.13 (a)); the fold release path joins the R1e LayoutError list.
rationale: Both places must be recognised during the transition, because existing repos keep the root copy until they migrate; doing it before the move keeps R3 a pure move.
rejected: Waiting for R3 and flipping rel() (sets would hold only the new place while repos keep the root copy); basename matching (widens the security sets); a single is_known_location predicate (regexes, pathspecs and frozensets need the list up front).
